profile.headline: Staff Embedded SWE @ Gecko Robotics
profile.summary:
Embedded systems engineer who wants to make the world a better place through thoughtful and intentional use of robotic technology. Detail oriented with a high bar of quality and passion for solving difficult problems. Engaged with business and product leaders to ensure that engineering investments are focused on real customer outcomes.

Experienced as a people lead and a senior IC. Skilled at deep dives into tech stacks for analysis and troubleshooting of complex systems. Architecture-minded. DevOps experience to provide tools and workflows for delightful developer experiences.

## Technical Achievements

- Created a Yocto Linux distribution targeting NVIDIA Jetson Orin SOMs, including BSP integration for multiple carrier boards, security hardening to DOD STIG, integration of FIPS cryptography modules, and build infrastructure for developer and production workflows. This work was essential towards compliance to unlock gov contracts at Gecko Robotics.
- Architected a firmware monorepo for STM32 microcontrollers used throughout Gecko Robotics. Created an in-application programming (IAP) system for firmware updates. Setup local and cloud build infra including Jenkins builds and linters / static analysis (including a subset of MISRA checks). Core developer of early firmware apps, libraries, and communication protocols. Transitioned into a maintainer role and guided junior engineers through an I2C -> CAN bus major hardware revision. FW monorepo has been in production use for over 7 years now including the TOKA, Monarch, and Komodo inspection systems.
- Solo developer for Rust libraries and application used for non-destructive testing of concrete assets with the Monarch inspection system. Full stack project from comm drivers down to hardware through frontend application using iced-rs.

## Skills

- Yocto Linux
- Basic kernel drivers
- Linux systems integration
- Microcontroller firmware and embedded systems software in C/C++, Python, Go, and Rust
- Robotics software with ROS2
- Real-Time design with Linux and RTOS
- Embedded DevOps (build systems, CMake, Jenkins, distributed system updates, fleet management, configuration management, telemetry and diagnostics)
- Distributed embedded systems communicating via I2C, SPI, UART, Ethernet, CAN, etc.
- PCB design including some high speed design (USB3)
- Power electronics, sensors, and actuators
- Docker and container orchestration applied to robotics applications
- Basic front-end development with React, Qt, and Iced-rs
- Basic proficiency with FPGAs and Verilog / VHDL

positions.title: Electrical Engineer
positions.description: Embedded firmware developer for industrial-grade motion controllers.

positions.title: Part-time Software Developer for Test Engineering
positions.description: Part-time control software developer for reliability testing fixtures.

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Worked on reliability engineering team to design and run accelerated life cycle testing fixtures for a next generation product development process.
- Designed and tested control software (written in C# and LabVIEW) used to run reliability test fixtures and to collect experimental data for development of probabilistic reliability models
- Created a library of reusable software components shared between test fixture applications to help reduce future development time for new fixture software.
- Wrote documentation regarding software design and assisted in writing reliability test plans
- Selected sensors and designed supporting circuitry used to take analog and digital measurements with MCC DAQ devices
- Designed, built, and tested a custom PCB adapter for USB to 3V3 UART/5V UART/RS-232 conversion

positions.title: Automation Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Worked with OMEGA's Development and Engineering Center (ODEC) to support automation efforts through mechanical design, 2D/3D CAD and drafting, and supplementary projects.

- Designed configurable, standardized part nest fixture system for semi-automation of thermocouple connector screw insertion.
- Fixed two design flaws with BX Cable Fish machine used to pull thermocouple wires through outer BX cable sheathing
- Worked on floor layouts and production flow planning to prepare for movement of machines from one building to another.
- Converted an initial 2D design of a new fine-gauge bare wire thermocouple bead welder to a full 3D model with detail drawings for each component and a complete BOM.
- Created an initial prototype design for a rotating connector pin sieve used to filter out bent connector pins before loading them into a vibrating feeder bowl for a larger machine.
- Performed research and setup to establish a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) in order to keep track of automation maintenance history/preventive maintenance.

positions.title: Production Management Intern
positions.description:
Summer Internship 2015: performed research and setup to implement Kanban for high volume materials used in production (screws, nuts, bolts, grommets, etc.)

- Performed sales and usage research using data from old VAX based system and recently adopted Infor SyteLine ERP.
- Setup 2-bin storage location for each Kanban item
- Helped with transition from old terminal system to ERP by correcting negative inventory. Corrected inventory counts and mistakes on job/item BOMs.

Winter 2016: returned to assist in data analysis for inventory relocation due to expansion of production at the NJ facility

- Determined highest volume materials used in certain production departments
- Calculated worst case quantity for stored materials
- Designed a general shelving layout and determined usage of space by stored materials

volunteerExperiences.description: Recurring volunteer for Wolverine BEST Robotics at Grove City College. Served in various roles including engineering notebook judge, robot judge, and competition referee.

Served as a Robot Design Judge at a 2015 FIRST LEGO League qualifier held at Salem Community College. Worked with two co-judges to judge a set of 8 FLL teams on the design of their robots, focused on the robot programming. Participated in the deliberation process and ranking of all 24 teams, leading to the decision of the recipient of the FLL Programming Award at the event.
